title: LLM Hallucination Detection via Low-rank Multilinear Decomposition
abstract: arXiv:2610.36191v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) frequently generate fluent yet factually incorrect responses, raising concerns about their reliability. Recent hallucination detectors increasingly exploit internal representations, but extracting informative signals from high-dimensional hidden states remains challenging. Existing approaches often rely on selected activations or pooling-based compression, potentially overlooking discriminative information distributed across Transformer layers, feature modes, and tokens. We propose LOTUS (Low-rank Order-statistic TUcker-based Subspace learning), a multilinear low-rank decomposition framework for hallucination detection that extracts compact representations from LLM hidden states while reducing dependence on labeled data. Our approach first summarizes variable-length token representations using complementary statistical descriptors that capture peak activations, activation distributions, and cross-layer change

translated_title: 基于低秩多线性分解的大语言模型幻觉检测
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）经常生成流畅但事实错误的回复，引发了对其可靠性的担忧。近期的幻觉检测器越来越多地利用内部表示，但从高维隐藏状态中提取有信息量的信号仍然具有挑战性。现有方法通常依赖于选择性激活或基于池化的压缩，可能忽略了分布在Transformer层、特征模式和词元中的判别信息。我们提出了LOTUS（基于低秩顺序统计量Tucker分解的子空间学习），这是一个用于幻觉检测的多线性低秩分解框架，能够从LLM隐藏状态中提取紧凑表示，同时减少对标注数据的依赖。我们的方法首先使用互补的统计描述符来汇总可变长度的词元表示，这些描述符捕捉峰值激活、激活分布和跨层变化……
tldr: 提出LOTUS框架，利用多线性低秩分解从大语言模型隐藏状态中提取紧凑表示，实现幻觉检测并减少对标注数据的依赖。
en_tdlr: LOTUS, a multilinear low-rank decomposition framework, extracts compact representations from LLM hidden states for hallucination detection while reducing dependence on labeled data.
